source_reviews.independent_solution: An honest observed candidate requires identifying the oscillator and periodic driver, then evidence that varying driving frequency relative to the system's natural response strengthens the motion. Large visible motion alone is insufficient to establish resonance. No personal observation may honestly be reported; a hypothetical illustration must not be represented as witnessed. Dangerous excitation is not required.

coverage.evidence: Source 1 maps only to choice-1. Evidence sufficiency remains central. Personal observation/example selection and real evidence collection/account organization are explicitly lost in the hypothetical recognition unit; the authentic open written question and complete nonunique answer remain separate.

source_reviews.independent_solution: In the unchanged linear door model, a constant force of 0.005 N produces only 0.005/50=0.0001 of the static displacement corresponding to 50 N and cannot hold the original open position. By repeatedly applying force in phase with motion, work per cycle can be positive and accumulate without dissipation, enabling gradual large motion in this ideal resonant model. Force values do not imply immediate opening, a specified opening time, or universal success with damping or nonlinear response.

coverage.evidence: Source 2 maps only to choice-2. The force values, dynamic/static distinction, timed net work, missing time data and arbitrary-dissipation limit all remain. Independent force-scheme design and written causal organization are the two declared losses.

source_reviews.independent_solution: With comparable driving strength and coupling, an approximately linear oscillator has a more pronounced resonant response at weak damping, driving frequency near the relevant natural frequency, and effective excitation of that mode. Finite build-up time and transient response must be distinguished from steady response; sustained resonant growth in an ideal undamped oscillator is not a universal real-system conclusion. Strong response does not by itself imply damage.

coverage.evidence: Source 3 maps only to choice-3. Weak damping, near-natural drive, coupling and damage limits are assessed jointly. The steady-response restriction does not test a learner-generated transient explanation; this is explicitly declared in limitations and coverage. Exact-undamped-growth and brief-push distinctions remain in the full open prompt/answer, not silently claimed as elicited by choices.

source_reviews.independent_solution: A valid new example must identify an energy source and state-dependent feedback that times replenishment of dissipated oscillation energy, without an externally independent periodic schedule. A possible example is a contact-interrupting electric buzzer: a battery energizes an electromagnet, armature movement changes the contact, and elastic return resets it; the state controls timing. A steady-airflow elastic reed is another conditional example when its vibration modulates flow and energy transfer. An energy source alone, externally timed motor drive, or repetition alone is insufficient. Novelty relative to all lesson examples will be checked after the blind phase, not guessed from unselected text.

coverage.evidence: Source 4 maps only to choice-4. The cart/control scheme is absent from the lesson's clock, balance-wheel, bell, organ-pipe/whistle and physiological examples. Original-example generation and independent mechanism design are explicitly lost; recognition is not called creation.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Free motion has no ongoing mechanical-energy input; its amplitude/energy follow initial conditions, decaying with damping but retaining amplitude in the undamped idealization. Forced steady periodic motion follows the independently prescribed drive frequency; amplitude depends on drive strength/frequency, natural properties and damping, with possible initial transients. Self-oscillation receives ongoing energy with state feedback controlling its timing; oscillator, source, feedback and dissipation jointly determine stable amplitude/frequency. Different starts can approach the same amplitude only if they reach the same stable state under unchanged conditions; arbitrary starts, multiple attractors and supply changes are not excluded. Amplitude decay alone cannot classify the three.

coverage.evidence: Source 5 maps only to choice-5. Energy, timing, frequency/amplitude, transients, ideal-free counterexample and same-stable-state conditions remain. Independent full three-way writing and counterexample production are explicitly lost. The compressed choice comparison is supplementary; explicit damped-free comparison remains in the current original prompt and full answer.
